# Istravex

> Open-source XDR conformance and replay kit for Stellar. Checks that SDKs decode and re-encode XDR faithfully, and that indexers store the right records for the right accounts, using a shared, versioned corpus of rare but valid Stellar XDR. Proposed for Stellar Community Fund (SCF) #46, RFP 2. Status: proposed for funding; a working prototype (corpus, runners, replay) is in the repository.

## Docs

- [Repository](https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex): site, corpus, capture scripts, runners, replay harness
- [Corpus format](https://github.com/hackcat29/istravex/tree/main/corpus): manifest schema and fixtures
- [Full proposal (Markdown)](/proposal.md): scope, problem, deliverables, draft manifest, milestones, maintenance
- [SCF RFP Track](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/rfp-track): official RFP scope

## Corpus today (real data)

- 4 fixtures, all captured from live networks (synthetic: false):
  - cap27-muxed-payment-pubnet-0001: mainnet ledger 65474279; USDC payment to muxed ID 1764988090084626463 (above 2^53; JavaScript Number() reads 1764988090084626400)
  - cap15-fee-bump-pubnet-0001: mainnet ledger 65474309; fee source differs from inner source; fee charged 40354 stroops vs 46340 debited in fee meta before the Soroban refund
  - cap40-signed-payload-signer-testnet-0001: testnet account LedgerEntryData with an ed25519 signed-payload signer
  - cap73-sac-trust-testnet-0001: testnet trustline created by SAC trust(), with no changeTrust op
- SDK conformance: @stellar/stellar-sdk 17.4.0, go-stellar-sdk 0.9.0, stellar-xdr 30.0.0 pass 36/36 checks (decode, byte-exact re-encode, native)
- Replay: the naive envelope-based indexer fails 3/3 cases (incorrect, incorrect, dropped); the metadata-based reference indexer gets 3/3 correct

## Deliverables

1. Versioned XDR corpus + CAP coverage audit (captured ledgers and pinned stellar-core recipes; synthetic entries labelled; checked against `--check-lcm` goldens where available)
2. Offline indexer replay harness (mock Stellar RPC `getLedgers`, reference adapter for `wallet-backend`; verdicts: correct, incorrect, dropped)
3. Cross-SDK conformance runner (pinned JavaScript, Go, Rust adapters; decode, byte-for-byte re-encode, native conversion checks; wide integers kept at full precision)
4. Go linter (3 rules: trusting Core pass-through fields; unbounded recursive XDR; participants derived from the envelope instead of ledger meta) + indexer-hardening guide
5. Upstream pilot against `wallet-backend` with a triaged findings report

## Manifest fields

id, cap_ids, protocol_version, network, xdr_type, xdr_path, sha256, source, synthetic, expected_decoded, expected_indexed. Wide integers are decimal strings.

## Milestones

1. Corpus and reference replay
2. Conformance and linting
3. Upstream pilot and public release

## Commitments (proposed)

Apache 2.0; named maintainer for 6 months after launch, through the first protocol upgrade after delivery; no usage telemetry.
